- "you" (likely a designer/ builder) -> role: Builder.
- "children" (group) -> role: Children.

Thus two lanes: Builder and Children.

1. Develop the basic design. (task)
2. Order certain Lego brick sets. (task)
3. Give the lego sets to a group of children which should sort the parts for you (into a number of containers). This is one activity? Could split: "Give the lego sets to children" and "Children sort the parts into containers". We'll treat as two tasks: "Give Lego sets to children" (Builder) and "Sort parts into containers" (Children). However description says "You give the lego sets to a group of children which should sort the parts for you". So maybe a single combined activity but should be separate because different actors; we can have a task "Give Lego sets to children" (Builder) then a task "Sort parts into containers" (Children).

4. Build subcomponents individually using parts from sorted containers. Activity: "Build subcomponents" (Builder). Might involve loop? Not necessary.

5. If there are no more parts in a container, you reorder individual parts. Decision after building each subcomponent? Actually after using parts, if container empty, reorder. This is a decision gateway with two branches: Yes (no parts) -> "Reorder individual parts" (Builder) then loop back to building? We'll model as exclusive gateway after "Build subcomponents" with condition "No more parts in container?" If yes, reorder; after reorder, go back to "Build subcomponents". If no, continue.

6. After building each subcomponent, you have to test them individually and (if each test is successful) assemble them. So after building subcomponent (and ensuring parts are available), we test subcomponent. Then decision: test successful? If yes, "Assemble subcomponents" (Builder) else "Redesign subcomponents" (Builder) then "Rebuild subcomponents" (Builder) then loop back to test? description: "If subcomponents are not tested successfully, you have to redesign and rebuild them." So after redesign and rebuild, probably need to test again. We'll model loop: after "Rebuild subcomponents", go back to "Test subcomponents". This decision loop until success then assemble. After assemble, maybe end process. So include end event after assembly.

Parallel? No parallel activities described. So only exclusive gateways.

Now make BPMN XML with laneSet and flow nodes.

Define IDs for elements: start event id "start". Tasks:

t1: developDesign

gateway1: checkNoParts (exclusive)
t6: reorderParts
gateway2: testResult (exclusive)
t7: testSubcomponent
t8: redesignSubcomponents

t10: assembleSubcomponents
endEvent id "end".

f1 start->t1
f2 t1->t2
f3 t2->t3
f4 t3->t4
f5 t4->t5
f6 t5->gateway1
gateway1 outgoing: 
- f7 yes (parts available) -> t7 (test) (maybe decision branching: if no more parts, reorder; else continue to test).
- f8 no (no parts) -> t6 (reorder parts). t6 goes back to t5 (build) maybe? So after reorder, we loop to t5. So f9 from t6 -> t5.

Now test branch: after t5 (if parts available) go to test t7.

Then after test, exclusive gateway2 testResult.

Gateway2 outgoing:
- f10 name "success" -> t10 (assemble)
- f11 name "failure" -> t8 (redesign)

After redesign, we need rebuild (t9) then go to test again (t7). So f12 from t8 -> t9, f13 from t9 -> t7.

After assemble t10 -> end.

Now assign lanes:

Builder lane includes tasks: developDesign, orderLegoSets, giveLegoSets, buildSubcomponents, reorderParts, testSubcomponent, redesignSubcomponents, rebuildSubcomponents, assembleSubcomponents.

Children lane includes task: sortParts.

Gateways belong to builder lane (or could be separate but need a lane). We'll assign them to builder lane.

Now produce XML according to reference.

Need to ensure each flow node referenced in lane via flowNodeRef.

Sequence flow IDs unique.

Will also include startEvent and endEvent as builder lane.

Now produce XML.
